blocks.text: British fine art photographer Julia Fullerton-Batten opened yesterday her exhibition The Theatre of Life at House of Photography in Stockholm. Her cinematic photographs are the result of extensive preparation, set design and lighting. The exhibition also reveals parts of the creative process behind the images.

Despite their almost surreal appearance, the photographs are created in front of the camera rather than digitally constructed in post-production. This is an important aspect of her artistic practice, one that Per Broman believes has taken on new significance today.

“I first worked with Julia in 2014. Back then, I could hardly have imagined how much our perception of photography would change in just twelve years. As AI-generated images become increasingly common, the craft of photography has taken on an entirely new significance. I appreciated Julia’s photographs even then, but today I find her work more relevant and her creative process more impressive than ever,” says Per Broman, CEO and founder of House of Photography.

Julia Fullerton-Batten is internationally recognised for her cinematic fine art photography. She creates elaborate scenes that are photographed like a still from a film or a fragment of a larger narrative. Unusual locations, street-cast models and cinematic lighting characterise her distinctive style. Her photographs suggest underlying tensions and evoke a sense of mystery that invites viewers to return to them.

Her subjects are often drawn from personal experiences, historical events and human stories. The preparation behind a single photograph can take several months. In The Theatre of Life, House of Photography also presents material from the creative process, offering visitors an insight into how her staged photographs come to life.
Julia Fullerton-Batten – The Theatre of Life November 25, 2026 – March 2027 House of Photography Sankt Paulsgatan 29 118 48 Stockholm, Sweden https://www.houseofphotography.se/en-int
